answer: Sequential-presence seats: a seat opens only after a 30-day voyage of one answer per day, and each day's topic is beacon-drawn after that day begins, so nothing can be precomputed. Arrivals register at one wharf per day, a single ordered queue that compares arrival fingerprints across every seat; two seats sharing a fingerprint are both slashed. Each seat locks a bond there, forfeit on a missed or replayed day. Ten seats need ten parallel calendars of real elapsed time, an oasis of supply no API key can compress, so attacker cost scales with heads times days, never with capital.
